# Luck, Location, or a Leak?

Management wants to replace its ten lowest-earning slots. We recommend inspecting one machine for $1,200 and retaining $98,800.

**Luck and exposure.** Nine of the bottom ten sit in Back Forty; three were on the floor for only part of January–June. We compare expected win per available hour, excluding off-floor days and preserving dated placements. Payout screens use published variance and actual bets, with a multiple-comparison threshold. M-1158 pays on 38.6% of spins versus 31.5% published. Inspect its meters and configuration; this is not proof of wrongdoing.

**Location.** We investigated all four movers against same-game machines that stayed in their original zone, excluding move days. M-1152’s Back Forty-to-Main Entrance move coincided with a 130% relative increase in theo/hour; its pointwise time-block interval is +106% to +161%. The other three intervals include no change. Nonrandom placement and redistribution prevent a property-profit claim.

**A competing explanation matters.** Back Forty already declined relative to other zones before the walkway closure: approximately 0.8% weekly. The closure comparison therefore fails a clean parallel-trends interpretation. We show the adverse diagnostic instead of attributing the entire drop to access.

**Downtime and guests.** Same-game, same-zone hourly peers imply about $102k forgone theo over six months before switching; 50% retention elsewhere reduces property loss to $51k. Tracked guests wagered $163.8M and received $148.2M. Comp redemption prices fell abruptly. A documented, deferred $4,000 pilot needs 10,288 players per arm and detects roughly $4.88 per assigned player under planning assumptions; non-returners remain included.

**Validation.** The unchanged January–April weekday model scores May–June MAE $68,699 versus $218,258 and R² 0.8803. Three earlier expanding-window backtests also beat baseline. Intervals calibrated only on February–April errors cover 59/61 holdout days; temporal dependence limits coverage guarantees. Schedule inspection on a quiet weekday after its lead time.

**Tradeoffs.** Inspection-only July contribution scenarios (no recovery / partial recovery with repair / larger recovery with repair) are −$1,224 / +$276 / +$3,276, including downtime and conditional repair allowances. These are assumptions, not guaranteed recovery. The former inspection/signage/pilot package loses about $8,832 in its base case after switching and costs; signage and the fully specified pilot remain unfunded options. The dashboard exposes filter scope, evidence, uncertainty and interactive spending assumptions.





Ace uses the Gemini API to rehearse feasible choices, select checked tradeoffs and challenge findings with retrieved evidence. Gameplay is fictional; the dashboard supports the actual recommendation.
